title: Per‑vector smoothing and bundled batch incentives pilot for rerank-heavy customers
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary: Propose and run a 6-week pilot that introduces a per-vector smoothing mechanism plus a bundled batch incentive for customers with high rerank/embedding volumes. Goal is to reduce billing volatility for customers with bursty ingestion patterns, capture upsell to committed batch slots, and measure unit economics impact on cost/revenue. This ticket covers experiment design, pricing formulas, QSA/legal intake for enterprise contracts, telemetry, and rollout gating.

Why now: Multiple enterprise prospects (anonymized: "Enterprise A" and "SearchCo") reported procurement friction due to per-vector price spikes when they rerank at large scale. Competitors are offering simple slab discounts; we can differentiate with time-smoothing + optional batch bundles that preserve unit economics while improving predictability.

Experiment design: Two parallel cohorts for 12 selected customers (6 pilot, 6 control) + open self-serve pilot offer in Console. Pricing treatments: 
- Treatment A (Smoothing only): bill per-vector but apply a 7-day exponential smoothing on per-day volumes with alpha=0.3; invoice uses smoothed daily vector count for per-vector billing.
- Treatment B (Smoothing + Bundled Batch Slots): same smoothing plus optional purchase of batch slots (bundles of 1M vectors) at a 12% unit discount relative to baseline per-vector price; unused vectors in a slot expire on a 30-day rolling window. Bundles are additive to regular usage.
- Control: current per-vector billing with existing batch credits pilot rules.

Pricing formulas (proposal): 
- Baseline per-vector price = $0.00085/vector for standard embedding model; rerank multipliers unchanged.
- Smoothed_invoice_vectors_day_t = round(alpha * actual_day_t + (1 - alpha) * smoothed_day_{t-1})
- If batch bundle purchased: price_per_vector_in_bundle = baseline * 0.88; consumption draws from bundle first, then smoothed invoice quantity for remaining.

Success metrics (primary): 
- Customer perceived billing volatility: reduce 7-day coefficient of variation of daily billed vectors by >=40% for Treatment A and >=60% for Treatment B. 
- Revenue neutrality target: pilot should not reduce Redwood net margin by >5% relative to matched baseline cohort over pilot window. 
- Adoption interest: >=25% of pilot customers offered bundles choose to purchase at least one slot.

Secondary metrics: churn signal, support ticket volume about invoices, average gross margin per vector, model inference cost delta (from runtime telemetry).

Telemetry & dashboards: New dashboards in Console -> Billing Experiments (dashboard link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PM/PM-886210-experiment-dashboard) showing per-customer smoothed vs actual, revenue delta, bundle uptake, support tickets (from Zendesk), and runtime cost signals (from infra-costs.jira link). Feature flags in prod controlled by flag: experiments.embed.smoothing.

QSA / Enterprise contract work: We will prepare a packaged addendum for enterprise customers that documents: pricing changes, auditability of smoothing math, expiration rules for bundles, data retention for billing logs, and an SLO for invoice correction (14-day dispute window). Legal has requested a QSA intake doc for security impact of new billing controls (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example-qsa). Action items: run security questionnaire (owner: Security — Priya Rao) and produce one-page summary for sales.

Implementation notes: Backend changes required in billing pipeline (billing-service) and metering: compute smoothed vectors in aggregation layer (job: bill-aggregation-v2). Billing exposure needs API changes for invoices to include "smoothed_count" and "bundle_consumed" fields. Console UI needs a small UX flow for purchasing bundles and a changelog entry for billing smoothing. Engineering estimate: 5 sprint points across billing & console teams.

Risk & mitigations: 
- Revenue leakage: cap bundle discounts in pilot and monitor gross margin; pilot cohort selection prioritized low-margin-high-volume customers under PM/Finance oversight.
- Support burden: create canned support responses and invoice breakdown export to CSV.
- Legal/regulatory: ensure smoothing math and expirations documented for QSA; commit to invoice reversals if math errors present.

Rollout plan & gating: 
- Week 0: internal design review + legal/QSA intake (done).
- Week 1–2: engineering implement metering and invoice fields behind feature flag.
- Week 3: QA + pilot cohort onboarding (6 customers) + open self-serve opt-in.
- Week 4–6: observe metrics; weekly readout with Finance.
- Gate to wider release: if primary metrics meet targets and Security signs off, ship as opt-in product feature in pricing-q2-2026 release.

Artifacts: Confluence PRD (https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PM/PM-886210), GitHub proposal PR for billing changes (#redwood/billing PR 2421), Console UI mocks in Figma (https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/embed-bundles), and sales one-pager (Drive link above).
